helper_scripts: code/parse_check_b02.py (machine check only; shards were written directly, not generated)

conventions.paragraph: one blank-line-separated block of the source (hard-wrapped lines joined); chapter heading line excluded; numbered 1-based within the chapter. id = chNNN-pNN, locator (source) = chNNN#pNN, plus lines [first,last] (1-based source-file line numbers). 2-digit width to match batches b01/b03 (all b02 chapters have < 100 paragraphs).
conventions.paragraph_text: verbatim source text (curly quotes, em dashes and _underscore_ italics markers kept). Prose: wrapped lines joined with a single space. Verse / stage-direction blocks (format: verse | stage_direction): lines joined with \n, leading indentation removed. Section-break asterisk rows kept as paragraphs with format: section_break.
conventions.scene: id = chNNN-scNN; source = chNNN#pNN-pNN (inclusive range); scenes cut on location / time / cast change, never inside a paragraph; boundary_reason gives the basis; location_cue / present / time_cue are surface cues taken from the text (not bible IDs).
conventions.dialogue: id = chNNN-dNNNN, sequential per chapter; one entry per utterance. text = the quoted words without the outer quote marks; when an utterance is interrupted by a narrative tag, the verbatim quoted pieces are listed in segments[] and text = the segments joined with one space. type: dialogue (spoken, incl. mode self_talk = 'said to herself'), thought ('thought Alice' etc.), verse (recited or sung stanza; the text is the whole stanza, with the poem's own quotation marks). mode also marks whisper_overheard / sung / sung_chorus / self_talk_then_aloud. speaker = readable surface-based label, speaker_key = tentative lowercase slug (NOT a canonical CHAR id), speaker_basis = explicit tag or inference reason; candidates[] given whenever the attribution is inferred rather than explicitly tagged.
conventions.group_speakers: speaker 'CROWD' (ch004, speaker_key crowd-rabbit-helpers) is used only where the text itself assigns the words to a group ('a good many voices', 'a general chorus', 'the others'); 'CHORUS' (ch006) follows the source label 'CHORUS. (In which the cook and the baby joined)'. These count as attributed, not UNKNOWN; individual voices inside them are not assigned.
conventions.entities: one entry per (paragraph, surface form): type person|place|item|skill, mention = exact surface string as written (checked as a substring of the paragraph), tentative_key = provisional slug for later unification by character-manager / worldbuilding. Talking animals are typed person (they speak/act as characters). Named or clearly nominal mentions only; pronouns and passing figures of speech (e.g. 'like a cart-horse', 'Jack-in-the-box') are not tagged. No 'skill' mentions occur in this batch.
conventions.inscriptions: written text visible in the scene (sign / label) is listed per scene in inscriptions[], not as dialogue.

coverage.method: shard_word_count = heading tokens + whitespace tokens of every paragraph text; each paragraph text compared (whitespace-normalised) with its source block; all 200 paragraphs identical to source.

inferred_attributions_below_0.95.speaker: CHORUS
inferred_attributions_below_0.95.basis: source label names cook + baby joining; Duchess implied

speaker_stats.cross_batch_references: none needed a cross-batch speaker; ch005-d0021 quotes the title of 'How doth the little busy bee' (recited in ch002, batch b01), which is recorded as an item mention only.

checks: schema keys present (chapter / scene / dialogue / entity)
paragraph count = source block count; ids and locators sequential; line ranges match
word counts reconcile with manifest and wc -w of the chapter range
scene source ranges match their paragraphs; boundary_reason present
every dialogue segment, entity mention and inscription is a substring of its cited paragraph and lies inside its scene
UNKNOWN ratio < 2% and every UNKNOWN has candidates
quote coverage: every “…” span in the text is covered by a dialogue or inscription entry

uncovered_quotes_intentional.reason: the text says this bottle has NO such label ('There was no label this time with the words “DRINK ME,”'); it is not present in the scene, so it is neither an inscription nor dialogue
narrator's note on how Pat said 'arm' ('He pronounced it “arrum.”'), not a separate utterance; kept in the paragraph text

decisions: Scene cuts (15 total): ch004 outside→Rabbit's room→siege (Rabbit arrives)→escape/puppy→mushroom; ch005 Caterpillar→alone with mushroom (+ asterisk section break)→Pigeon above the treetops→little house; ch006 footmen→Frog-Footman at the door→kitchen→baby/pig→Cheshire Cat→March Hare's house.
'the Footman' in ch006 p06-p17 is attributed to Frog-Footman (0.97): p04 states the Fish-Footman was gone and 'the other' sat by the door.
ch004 p24/p27/p29 crowd lines are kept as group utterances (CROWD) instead of being split to guessed individuals.
'You are old, Father William' is logged as 8 verse entries spoken by Alice (the reciter) with in_verse_speaker per stanza; the Duchess's lullaby is 2 sung stanzas + 2 CHORUS entries.

Inner-debate ambiguity: ch004-d0011 ('she answered herself') is typed dialogue/self_talk by its verb, with type_note; ch006-d0035 is typed thought, with a note that its last words were said out loud. Downstream can reclassify both.
notes_for_p0_merge: Scene-level field names differ across the parallel batches because no shared shard schema was given: b01 uses location/time/cast_present/paragraph_range/quoted_text; b02 uses location_cue/time_cue/present/inscriptions; b03 uses setting/present. The shared keys (chapter id/title/word_count/scenes; scene id/boundary_reason/source/paragraphs/dialogues/entities; dialogue id/type/speaker/speaker_confidence/text/source; entity type/mention/source) line up. p0-merge assembles shards without rewriting them, so if a single scene schema is wanted, orchestrator should rule on one and send it back to the batches.
b02 chapter shards carry _meta (b03 uses _shard); chapter file/line range is under source{} (b01 has top-level file/line_start/line_end).
